sections.h2: Your choices for a fast exit
sections.html:
You can hire a broker, sell privately on your own, or accept a cash proposal. Of the three, only cash skips a lender's approval, so it moves fastest against a hard deadline.

Harker Heights has 35,195 residents, and many work in Killeen or at Fort Cavazos. That ties numerous sales to job moves and orders, so closing dates carry extra weight. Get every interested buyer to commit to a funding date in writing, and treat a vague "a few weeks" as no answer. Moving on orders? Tell buyers, and ask who can close around your report date. Flexibility on timing is worth more than a few extra dollars from a buyer who cannot meet it.

  • Broker listing: for a tidy house and an owner who can tolerate showings and a buyer's financing.
  • Private sale: fits owners who already know a buyer and can manage contracts and title work.
  • Cash proposal: for houses needing work, empty houses and owners racing a move date.

Harker Heights started as a 1957 plat along U.S. Highway 190 east of Killeen and became a bedroom community served by the Killeen Independent School District. Population was 26,700 in 2010, 33,097 in 2020 and 35,195 for 2025. Fast growth means most houses are newer subdivision stock, so your buyer will compare yours with others built in the same years.

Nearby draws that families often ask about include the Killeen Municipal Golf Course and Stillhouse Hollow Lake. Say so in your description of the house if any of them is a short drive away.

The city covers 15.61 square miles of land. Voters approved incorporation on September 24, 1960, once a water system was finished, and a December 1988 annexation of the 2,200-acre Comanche Hills utility district grew the townsite from 4,400 acres to 6,600. Lots platted in different decades can carry different easements and setbacks, so a current survey helps a buyer feel sure about boundaries.

Owners live in 61.7% of homes, and the midpoint value is $287,800 for 2020 to 2024. Both are citywide numbers, so a house on a quiet cul-de-sac could land higher or lower.

The average household has 2.72 people, and 85.5% of residents were at the same address a year earlier, which suggests settled families. Buyers tend to ask about bedrooms, yard size and school zones. Some buyers and sellers are military households who need a closing that fits an orders deadline.

The Tax Appraisal District of Bell County sets your value, and the bill that follows stays with the property. Bills mail near October 1. Whatever remains unpaid after January 31 becomes delinquent, and from February 1 a 6% penalty and 1% interest apply. The penalty then grows 1% monthly until it reaches 12% on July 1, and a collection attorney, if hired, may add as much as 20%.

  • Homeowners may pay half by November 30 and half by June 30.
  • Order the tax certificate from the Bell County tax office, because the appraisal district does not issue one.
  • Check with the appraisal district on which exemptions sit on your account and whether they end when the deed transfers.

Funding waits until the title company sees this year's bill paid, so settle any back balance early. If a balance is left over, have the title officer show where it will be deducted from your proceeds before you sign.

Selling is possible once the title shows who owns the house. Texas gives families four years after a death to probate a will. If the estate needs no administrator, the will plus a court order is recorded as a muniment of title at the clerk's office in the county where the land lies.

Modest estates may use a small estate affidavit instead. It requires no will, no petition for administration, assets of $75,000 or less outside the homestead, agreement from every heir, and a judge's approval. A transfer on death deed, if the owner recorded one before dying, hands the house to named beneficiaries with no probate.

Start by collecting the death certificate, any will and the newest tax statement. Staff in the Bell County clerk's probate office can point you to the right filing, and the buyer's title company will want to see it recorded before closing.

Call the city's Planning and Development department about permits for any added room, deck, carport or garage conversion. Inspectors and title companies spot unpermitted work, and it can slow a deal or shrink an offer.

Did you ever host guests there? Phone the city and find out whether a rental registration exists that you should cancel before closing. Tell every buyer about open items. Some cash buyers take open items as they come; a buyer with a mortgage may demand fixes before funding.

sections.h2: Papers to gather before you take offers
sections.html:
A thin folder now saves days later. Begin with the recorded deed and your newest Bell County tax statement, then add each lender's payoff letter, the tax certificate once ordered, and permit records for work done since you bought.

If the house sits in the former Comanche Hills utility district, which the city absorbed in December 1988, ask the title company whether older utility easements show on the plat. If someone is renting from you, add the lease and deposit record, and decide whether the buyer will inherit the tenant or receive the house vacant.

Ask each buyer for a written offer showing price, closing date, who pays closing charges and what happens to the earnest money if the deal collapses. Line the offers up and compare what you would keep after payoffs. A slightly lower figure with a firm date can beat a higher one that hangs on a loan.

With cash there is no loan approval, no lender appraisal and no repair haggling after an inspection. Title work remains, though: the record gets searched, payoffs get requested and a deed and settlement statement get drafted.

Settle three points before signing: the closing date, who pays title and recording charges, and whether you may stay a few days after funding. Keep copies of the contract and every notice you received, and release the keys only once the title company confirms the money has arrived. Clear out belongings, remove trash and leave the yard tidy, since a cash buyer's final walkthrough often happens the day before closing.

faqs.q: Must I fix the house before a cash buyer will make an offer?
faqs.a: No. A cash buyer prices the house in its present state. A broker listing typically needs more work, since a financed buyer orders an inspection and asks for fixes.

faqs.q: When does Bell County property tax become late?
faqs.a: Once January 31 passes with a balance open. Bills go out near October 1, and penalty and interest begin February 1. The Bell County tax office can quote your exact balance and any installment option.

faqs.q: Which office files my Harker Heights deed?
faqs.a: The Bell County clerk. A notary must witness your signature, and the title company normally carries the signed deed to the clerk after closing.

faqs.q: Can heirs list the house while probate is still open?
faqs.a: Usually only with legal authority, such as a court order or an executor's deed. A recorded transfer on death deed or a muniment of title order can also work. Check with a Texas attorney or the clerk's office first.

faqs.q: Is $287,800 what my house will sell for?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. It is a citywide midpoint for 2020 to 2024. Condition, size and street drive your price, so gather written offers and compare them with your Bell County appraisal account.
